produced_by: the collate side (lane-f) -- trainbench/collate.py, today scripts/bench.py
consumed_by: the measurement side (lane-d) -- the measured loop and trainbench/metrics/
owned_by: neither lane; change it only by agreement, and the contract test is what makes the change loud
how_the_payloads_were_produced: the four collates on this repo's rows below, through a deterministic stand-in processor (word ids = 3 + sum(ord(c)) % 997, pad id 0). The processor is a stub because it is the external dependency; the collates are real. tests/contract/test_collate_metrics.py rebuilds these and compares.

rows.pos_text: the red panda is a small mammal
eight thousand eight hundred forty nine metres

why_tensors_may_add_is_grouped: the keys a collate may put into tensors beyond the ones frozen per payload, split by the kernel each group gates. varlen_attention is all-or-nothing: modeling_flash_attention_utils.py:761-763 takes the varlen path only on all(kwarg is not None for kwarg in (cu_seq_lens_q, cu_seq_lens_k, max_length_q, max_length_k)), so three of four is a dense forward pass reported as a packed one. packed_conv is not part of that rule: Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet passes seq_idx and nothing else to causal_conv1d_fn (modeling_qwen3_5.py:492-499), so it is a separate gate on a separate kernel and holding it to the varlen four would make either group's absence look like the other's. The two were one flat list until seq_idx was added, which is why the groups exist.

fields.name: tensors
fields.meaning: exactly what goes to model(**tensors), keyed by the model's own kwarg names. No accounting number and no packing boundary may appear here: the model would reject them, and a count that travelled inside tensors would be moved to the device and read back inside the timed window.

fields.name: tokens
fields.meaning: REAL tokens: the ones the model does work on. Padding is excluded. This is the numerator the harness divides by measured seconds; it is never a framework's own tokens/sec and never padded_tokens.

fields.name: padded_tokens
fields.meaning: every token SLOT in the batch, padding included -- input_ids.numel(). Reported beside tokens so the padding fraction is visible; the packing axis reverses rank depending on which of the two is used as the denominator, so neither field may stand in for the other.

fields.name: rows
fields.meaning: how many SEQUENCES the batch stands for -- 2 per pair, queries then positives. This is not tensors['input_ids'].shape[0]: a packed batch is one tensor row holding every sequence, and there rows comes from the packing boundaries.

fields.name: samples
fields.meaning: how many dataset rows (query/positive pairs) the batch drew. rows == 2 * samples for every collate here. Distinct from rows because packing and pairing both make them differ, and in-batch negatives make the sequence count part of the objective.

fields.name: images
fields.meaning: images actually handed to the processor and paid for in the forward pass.

fields.name: images_dropped
fields.meaning: images present in the rows that this batch could not carry -- a text-only processor, or a packed/pretokenized path that carries ids only. Non-zero means the run measured a text-only view of an image corpus and the result has to say so.

fields.name: cu_seqlens
fields.meaning: the packing boundary: a 1-D vector of rows+1 cumulative REAL-token offsets, starting at 0 and ending at tokens. Present if and only if the batch is packed. null is what tells the step to pool the padded way, so an absent-but-packed batch would be pooled at the wrong positions.

fields.name: images_per_row
fields.meaning: how many of the flat pixel batch each of the rows sequences contributed, in batch order; len == rows and sum == images. null means no batch of this shape carries pixels at all, which is not the same as a tuple of zeros (this batch happened to carry none) -- the splitter refuses on null rather than assuming.

invariants: padded_tokens == number of token slots in tensors['input_ids']
tokens == tensors['attention_mask'].sum() when the batch carries a mask
tokens == padded_tokens when the batch carries no mask (packed: no padding by construction)
cu_seqlens is not null if and only if the batch is packed
images_per_row is null, or len(images_per_row) == rows and sum(images_per_row) == images
no key of tensors is an accounting field name or a packing boundary name
every accounting field is an int, never a rate: the payload carries counters and the measurement side computes tokens/sec from them
of tensors_may_add.varlen_attention, either all four are present or none are (transformers takes the fast path only when all four are non-None)
tensors_may_add.packed_conv is outside that rule: seq_idx gates its own kernel and is judged by the four lines below alone
seq_idx is in tensors if and only if the batch is packed
seq_idx is int32 and has exactly the shape of tensors['input_ids'] -- one index per token slot
seq_idx[0] starts at 0, never decreases, and ends at rows - 1
seq_idx[0] changes value exactly at the cu_seqlens boundaries, so the segments it marks are the pack's sequences and not some other cut

padded_text_only.collate: Collate, text-only processor -- every image is counted as dropped
